topic: The Apollo Guidance Computer by the numbers
title: The Apollo Computer In Four Numbers #siliconverdict #apollo #bythenumbers
description: The Apollo Guidance Computer that helped land humans on the Moon, told through four numbers: memory, program, weight and power.
pinned_comment: Impressive or old? Reply with one word.

scenes.narration: The computer that reached the Moon had less memory than a photo.
Stay to the end, because the last number is the strangest one.
Its working memory held just 2048 words, roughly four kilobytes.
Engineers wrote the code by hand to fit, counting every single word.
The program itself lived in 36,864 words of woven wire memory.
Workers literally wove the software into wires, so a bug could not be patched.
The whole unit weighed about 32 kilograms, small enough to fly in a spacecraft.
It ran at roughly two megahertz, yet it navigated people all the way to the Moon.
And the last number: it drew only about 55 watts, like a bright light bulb.
Tight limits forced engineers to write brilliantly careful code.
Follow for more tech. Is that impressive, or just old?
